intro.data: One pipeline A→B→C→D must process TWO batches — a near batch (3) and a far batch (5) — into their true reports. Bring whatever faithful pieces you like: the three steps Double (x2), Shift (+3), Twin (x2), or a bundle plus a step. Grouping is free, so a faithful (g∘f) bundle then Twin works just as well as all three steps. But the tray hides a sly bundle 'Premix' that matches the real (g∘f) on the near batch and drifts on the far one — it passes the easy case and fails the hard one. Build the chain that nails BOTH batches and leave the look-alikes in the tray.

Bring whatever faithful pieces you like: the three steps Redouble (x2), Infuse (+3), Mirror (x2), or a bundle plus a step. Grouping is free, so a faithful (g∘f) bundle then Mirror works as well as all three steps. But the tray hides a sly bundle 'Premix' that matches the real (g∘f) on the near charge and drifts on the far one — passing the easy case and failing the hard one. Build the chain that nails BOTH charges and leave the look-alikes in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: One rite A→B→C→D must bind TWO sparks — a near spark (3) and a far spark (5) — into their true wards. Bring whatever faithful runes you like: the three steps Redouble (x2), Infuse (+3), Mirror (x2), or a bundle plus a step. Grouping is free, so a faithful (g∘f) bundle then Mirror works as well as all three steps. But the tray hides a sly bundle 'Premix' that matches the real (g∘f) on the near spark and drifts on the far one — passing the easy case and failing the hard one. Build the chain that nails BOTH sparks and leave the look-alikes in the tray.
intro.abstract: Here numbers are the carried values and a prime b′ is a different value of the same type. One A→B→C→D chain must satisfy two cases over the same start A and goal D: case 1 sends 3 ↦ 18, case 2 sends 5 ↦ 26. Compose f (×2), g (+3), h (×2); associativity makes h ∘ (g ∘ f), (h ∘ g) ∘ f, and h ∘ g ∘ f equal, so any faithful grouping works. But (g∘f)? (+6) coincides with g ∘ f at 3 (both give 9) so it passes case 1, while at 5 it gives 11 not 13 and fails case 2. Build the one chain that passes both and leave the impostors in the tray.

goal.data: Bring faithful steps or a faithful bundle from the tray and wire ONE pipeline that turns batch 3 into report 18 AND batch 5 into report 26.
goal.alchemy: Bring faithful steps or a faithful bundle from the tray and wire ONE process that turns charge 3 into alloy 18 AND charge 5 into alloy 26.
goal.spellcraft: Bring faithful runes or a faithful bundle from the tray and wire ONE rite that turns spark 3 into ward 18 AND spark 5 into ward 26.
goal.abstract: Place B and/or C and wire any faithful grouping of f, g, h so it sends 3 ↦ 18 and 5 ↦ 26, leaving the impostor bundle behind.

afterSuccess.data: However you grouped the faithful steps — all three (Double, Shift, Twin), or the faithful Prep bundle then Twin, or Double then the Finish bundle — both batches landed on their true reports: 3 to 18 and 5 to 26. That is associativity: regrouping never changes the result. 'Premix' had the right type and even matched the real bundle on the near batch, but it added 6 instead of bundling x2 then +3, so it drifted to 22 on the far batch and fell out. The far batch is why a bundle must genuinely BE the composite it claims, not merely agree once: (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f).
afterSuccess.alchemy: However you grouped the faithful steps — all three, or Prime then Mirror, or Redouble then Forge — both charges reached their true alloys: 3 to 18 and 5 to 26. That is associativity: regrouping never changes the result. 'Premix' had the right type and matched the real bundle on the near charge, but it added 6 instead of x2 then +3, drifting to 22 on the far charge. The far charge is why a bundle must genuinely be the composite: (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f).
afterSuccess.spellcraft: However you grouped the faithful runes — all three, or Prime then Mirror, or Redouble then Seal — both sparks reached their true wards: 3 to 18 and 5 to 26. That is associativity: regrouping never changes the result. 'Premix' had the right type and matched the real bundle on the near spark, but it added 6 instead of x2 then +3, drifting to 22 on the far spark. The far spark is why a bundle must genuinely be the composite: (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f).
afterSuccess.abstract: Every faithful grouping sent 3 ↦ 18 and 5 ↦ 26: h ∘ (g ∘ f) = (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ g ∘ f. (g∘f)? = +6 coincides with g ∘ f at 3 (both give 9), so it passed case 1, but at 5 it gives 11 not 13 and h then sends it to 22, failing case 2. Associativity lets you bundle freely — but only when each bundle is the true composite, and two cases prove it is.

reveal.summary: Associativity, under two test cases: (h ∘ g) ∘ f = h ∘ (g ∘ f) = h ∘ g ∘ f, so any grouping of the faithful steps reaches the goal — but a bundle that merely coincides with the real composite on one input still corrupts another, so two cases pin its behavior.
reveal.moreFormal: Composition is associative, so chains need no parentheses: h ∘ g ∘ f is unambiguous. A pre-bundled sub-step is interchangeable with its steps only when it equals their composite on every input.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: compose(compose(h, g), f) === compose(h, compose(g, f)); a precomputed sub-step can match on one test input yet still be the wrong function — a second case catches it.
